item.description: China has pulled off two-way laser communication between Earth and the moon, making it only the second nation after the United States to do so. But the data rates it achieved were well behind those recorded by Nasa more than a decade ago, and that has left space experts scratching their heads. Using telescopes in Yunnan province and an experimental satellite that is now orbiting the moon after a launch mishap in 2024, the team recorded a downlink speed of 100 megabits per second and an uplink... In June, it went a step further, bringing many of them together in a white paper on global governance and setting out how its Global Governance Initiative should translate principles into practice. Two ambitions sat side by side: an “equal and orderly multipolar world” and a “universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalisation”. The timing is telling. item.title: Agentic AI accelerates search for crops that can harvest critical minerals
item.description: For too long, the United States has relied on foreign sources for most of the raw materials powering its technological future: the essential minerals in every smartphone, battery pack and semiconductor. What if one answer to the supply crisis isn't buried in a mine shaft but growing quietly in a field? Scientists are betting on a resource-efficient, highly effective strategy: using engineered plants and symbiotic microbes to absorb critical minerals directly from the Earth in a process called phytomining. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Un alto funcionario de la Administración Trump se refirió al acuerdo petrolero con Venezuela, destacando el papel que cumple al fotalecer la hegemonía de EE. UU. en el hemisferio, desplazando a Rusia y China de campos clave. Por otro lado, se refirió a Alejandro Betancourt, empresario con investigaciones en Europa, que emergió como figura central del pacto. Por último, destacó que no hay condiciones para una transición democrática inmediata en Venezuela, aunque se prevén cambios a futuro. item.title: Canada's Labrador Shelf preserves climate records once thought erased by ice
item.description: The Labrador Shelf is a shallow marine area on the margin of the Labrador Sea in the North Atlantic off the east coast of Canada. item.title: Florida couple spent 41 years preserving a 1908 house; it is now a local historic landmark
item.description: In Oneco, Florida, the Johnson Helm House has earned the title of the first local historic landmark in the county. Built in 1908, this charming residence has been lovingly preserved by Margi and Pat Nanney for over four decades, keeping its unique architectural attributes intact. Their commitment has prevented modern alterations from obscuring its character, while this recognition emphasizes the area's important agricultural history. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
